page: Microsoft Azure D16ds_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL x86_64 processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The processor includes a 35 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

For local storage, the server includes a bundled 614 GB SSD and supports Premium Storage. In benchmark evaluations, the D16ds_v4 demonstrates mid-range performance. Its single-core stress-ng CPU score is 1425.48, while the multi-core score reaches 14891.9. Memory performance is characterized by a cached read-only bandwidth of 831.03 GB/sec, which drops to 79.84 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, and a write speed of 45.97 GB/sec. Database operations under Passmark score at 5724.25, and Redis SET operations achieve 14.01 million operations per second.

The hardware configuration offers a balanced resource density, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for standard enterprise workloads that require local scratch space without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. However, its performance on complex tasks is limited; for example, LLM inference on a medium 7B model drops to a weak 24.63 tokens/sec for prompt processing. Consequently, this server is recommended for general-purpose workloads, software compilation (scoring 12856.0 on Geekbench), static web serving (12.0 GB/sec throughput), and moderate database operations.
description: The Microsoft Azure D16ds_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine from the DDSv4 family, powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL x86_64 processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores) running at 2.6 GHz, 64.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 614 GB local SSD. Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance delivers balanced compute and memory resources. Benchmark results place its performance in the average tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 7781.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 15859.67. It achieves a static web serving throughput of 12.0 GB/sec and handles 14.01 million Redis SET operations per second. Lacking a GPU, it is not designed for heavy AI workloads, as shown by its weak 24.63 tokens/sec prompt processing on 7B LLM models. The D16ds_v4 is recommended for general-purpose enterprise applications, software compilation, and moderate database workloads.
